key_insight: Supervising real-space representations with electron density improved molecular energy prediction, but gains depended on the dataset.
engineering_relevance: Charge-density-informed models could improve atomistic energy prediction while providing spatial electronic information for materials analysis.
method: Train an equivariant graph neural network jointly on energy and valence electron density.
Integrate density-supervised real-space probe representations into the global energy regressor.
Analyze attention weights to identify influential probe locations.
evidence_signal: CDGNN reduced energy errors versus an equivariant GNN baseline on QM9 interpolation and larger-molecule extrapolation, matched baseline performance on small H-containing Fe and Fe-C datasets, and accurately predicted density distributions.
watch_item: Density supervision requires electron-density training data and does not guarantee improved energy accuracy across material systems.
paper_title: Charge density-supervised real-space representations for atomistic energy prediction
